title: Groups of Order pq: the Cyclic (Unique) Case when q ∤ (p−1)
description: For distinct primes p > q, a finite group of order p·q with q ∤ (p−1) is cyclic, and hence there is exactly one isomorphism class of such groups (all are ℤ/pq). This settles one direction of the biprimal isomorphism-class count: the parent open question asks for exactly 2 classes when q ∣ (p−1) and 1 otherwise; this entry proves the '1 class' case completely. The Sylow counting (n_r = 1 for every prime r) is done by hand, and cyclicity is obtained by routing through Mathlib's Z-group + nilpotency theory.

originalContributions: card_sylow_eq_one_of_card_pq: for every prime r, the number of Sylow r-subgroups of a group of order p·q (p>q, q∤(p−1)) equals 1 — proved by hand from n_r ∣ p·q, r ∤ n_r, n_r ≡ 1 [MOD r], plus the structural triviality of Sylow subgroups for primes not dividing the order.

isCyclic_of_card_pq: a finite group of order p·q with q ∤ (p−1) is cyclic — the '1 isomorphism class' direction of the biprimal classification, obtained by combining the Sylow count (all Sylows normal ⇒ nilpotent) with the squarefree Z-group structure.
unique_isoclass_of_card_pq: any two such groups are isomorphic (both ≅ ℤ/pq), via mulEquivOfCyclicCardEq.

overview.historicalContext: The classification of groups of order pq is a classical application of the Sylow theorems: when q ∤ (p−1) the group is forced to be cyclic, and when q ∣ (p−1) there is in addition a unique nonabelian semidirect product ℤ/p ⋊ ℤ/q. The parent entry (sylow-theorems-oq-01-oq-02) formalized the squarefree-order structure (every such group is a semidirect product of cyclic groups) but explicitly left the count of isomorphism classes open. This entry settles the cyclic (q ∤ p−1) direction of the biprimal count.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that a finite group of order p·q (p > q primes) with q ∤ (p−1) is cyclic, establishing that there is exactly one isomorphism class of groups of this order.
keyInsights: Sylow's third theorem gives n_r ≡ 1 [MOD r] and r ∤ n_r; together with n_r ∣ p·q this forces n_p = 1 (using q < p) and, when q ∤ (p−1), n_q = 1.
For a prime r not dividing |G|, every Sylow r-subgroup is trivial, so there is a unique (hence normal) one — this handles the universal quantifier over all primes needed by the nilpotency criterion.
All Sylow subgroups normal ⇒ G is nilpotent (Mathlib's isNilpotent_of_finite_tfae).
|G| = p·q is squarefree, so G is a Z-group (all Sylow subgroups cyclic); a finite nilpotent Z-group is cyclic.
Two cyclic groups of equal order are isomorphic, giving uniqueness of the isomorphism class.

conclusion.summary: A finite group of order p·q with p > q prime and q ∤ (p−1) is cyclic, so exactly one isomorphism class of groups of that order exists. This is the '1 class' half of the biprimal isomorphism-class count, proved as a fully verified (0-axiom) result. The Sylow count n_r = 1 for every prime r is established by hand; cyclicity then follows from the squarefree Z-group structure together with nilpotency.
openQuestions: The complementary case q ∣ (p−1): prove there are exactly 2 isomorphism classes (cyclic ℤ/pq and a unique nonabelian semidirect product ℤ/p ⋊ ℤ/q). This requires an isomorphism classification of semidirect products, not yet available in Mathlib.
Generalize the explicit count to squarefree order n = p₁···pₖ in terms of the divisibility relations pᵢ ∣ (pⱼ − 1).
